doc.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Miles Davis replaces him in the Benny Carter band
summary: Miles Davis, a kid from East St. Louis, took his place with Carter before he joined Hawkins.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: A lot of people didn’t know that. The morning that Benny left to go to Hollywood to do that movie — one of the big movies, I can’t think of the lady’s name — but anyway he got his break and he went and Miles was just a kid from East St. Louis. And he was downstairs waiting to see Benny then. Benny took him out west with him, and then I joined after that — I’m trying to think when I go back — then I joined Erskine Hawkins, that’s when, after that. I wasn’t too particular about joining Erskine Hawkins. I’ll tell you the bands that I liked, and I never really got a chance to play with them too much. I liked Don Redman’s band. I thought that Don Redman’s band was like perfect almost, like you know, because you know with Taft Jordan, Dick Vance and all those great trumpet players.
